evals.name: chromatography-class
evals.prompt: Preciso de uma animação para minha aula de química analítica mostrando como uma coluna de cromatografia separa dois compostos: a mistura é injetada, os dois compostos andam pela coluna com velocidades diferentes (um interage mais com a fase estacionária) e, conforme saem da coluna, vão desenhando dois picos no cromatograma ao lado. Texto na tela em português. Quero conseguir pausar e explicar cada etapa durante a aula. Me entrega em MP4, sem .pptx.
evals.expected_output: Stepwise animation (scenes/steps with a pause after each), MP4 1080p, cut into clips at the pauses with a pause sheet; Portuguese on-screen text; the compound that interacts more with the stationary phase elutes later and its peak is drawn as it leaves the column.
assertions: Delivers an MP4 video at 1920x1080, H.264, yuv420p
The video is cut into at least 4 clips
Every clip ends on a still frame (last frame equals the frame 0.1 s before)
Clips join seamlessly (last frame of each clip = first frame of the next)
On-screen text is in Portuguese
The compound that interacts more with the stationary phase moves slower and elutes later, and its peak is drawn in the chromatogram as it leaves the column (column and chromatogram share one clock)
Each teaching step ends in a pause (one clip per step) and the user is told how to change the pauses

evals.name: gradient-descent-readme-gif
evals.prompt: Faz um GIF curto (uns 10 segundos) pro README do meu repositório de otimização mostrando o gradiente descendente achando o mínimo de uma função de duas variáveis, com as curvas de nível e o caminho dos passos. Texto em inglês.
evals.expected_output: A short GIF (~10 s, README-sized) of real gradient descent steps on contour lines, English text; built in steps; clips optional.
assertions: Delivers a GIF
GIF lasts between 6 and 15 s
GIF is README-sized: width <= 1000 px and file <= 8 MB
GIF loops forever
GIF holds its final state for at least 1 s before looping
The path comes from a real gradient-descent computation (gradient evaluated at every step), not drawn by hand
On-screen text is in English

evals.name: calibration-curve-pptx
evals.prompt: Tenho os dados da curva de calibração da cafeína em calibracao_cafeina.csv (concentração em mg/L e área do pico). Anima a construção da curva para a minha apresentação de amanhã: os padrões aparecendo, a reta ajustada, a equação e o R², e no final a concentração de uma amostra desconhecida com área 48210. Vou apresentar no PowerPoint, então já me entrega os trechos com pausas num .pptx. Texto em português.
evals.expected_output: MP4 + clips at pauses + a .pptx with one slide whose stacked clips play one per click under the title; slope, intercept, R² and the unknown concentration computed from the CSV (not typed in); Portuguese text.
assertions: Delivers an MP4 video at 1920x1080, H.264, yuv420p
The video is cut into at least 4 clips
Every clip ends on a still frame (last frame equals the frame 0.1 s before)
Clips join seamlessly (last frame of each clip = first frame of the next)
Delivers a .pptx with the video's clips stacked on one slide
Clip 1 plays on the first click; each next click shows the next clip and plays it at the same moment (with previous)
The videos sit below the slide's title
Slope, intercept, R² and the unknown concentration on screen are computed from the CSV (≈4721.5, ≈637, R² ≈ 0.9999, ≈10.08 mg/L), not typed in
On-screen text is in Portuguese

evals.name: asks-what-to-deliver
evals.prompt: Faz uma animação mostrando como a busca binária encontra um número numa lista ordenada de 16 elementos. Texto em inglês.
evals.expected_output: Before planning or rendering, the skill asks which deliverable the user wants (.gif, .mp4 or both) and, for .mp4, whether to also build the .pptx deck and, for the deck, whether the title follows the CEMEP standard; it asks nothing about size, frame rate or other defaults.
assertions: Before rendering anything, asks which format the user wants (.gif, .mp4 or both)
Offers the .pptx deck as an option for the .mp4
Asks, for the deck, whether the title follows the CEMEP standard (blue bar, white title, CEMEP symbol) or is plain
Does not ask about size, frame rate or other defaults

evals.name: chromatography-timeline-pptx
evals.prompt: Anima uma linha do tempo da história da cromatografia para a minha aula: de Tswett (1903) até a HPLC e a GC-MS, com os marcos aparecendo um a um e um zoom quando chegar no período mais recente. Quero o MP4 e o .pptx com os trechos. Texto em português.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the timeline style; milestones enter one per step alternating above and below the axis, earlier ones dim, the axis zooms into the recent period; MP4 + clips + the click deck; dates checked, with sources in the docstring; Portuguese text.
assertions: Delivers an MP4 video at 1920x1080, H.264, yuv420p
The video is cut into at least 4 clips
Every clip ends on a still frame (last frame equals the frame 0.1 s before)
Clips join seamlessly (last frame of each clip = first frame of the next)
Delivers a .pptx with the video's clips stacked on one slide
Clip 1 plays on the first click; each next click shows the next clip and plays it at the same moment (with previous)
The videos sit below the slide's title
Starts from the timeline style (styles/timeline/timeline.py)
Milestones enter one per step, alternating above and below the axis
Earlier milestones dim when a new one enters
The axis zooms into the recent period at least once
Dates on screen are checked, with sources in the script's docstring
On-screen text is in Portuguese
